title: Teppan Shrimp and Pork Belly Mixed Grill
displayTitle: Teppan Shrimp and Pork Belly Mixed Grill
seoTitle: Teppan Shrimp and Pork Belly Mixed Grill | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Hibachi mixed grill—shrimp and pork belly, not the chicken-steak repeat
subtitle: Shrimp, pork belly, and griddled vegetables with ginger sauce for ten
description: Jumbo shrimp and pork belly cubes griddle with zucchini, mushrooms, and onions, finished with ginger-garlic sauce and sesame. Served with fried rice.

steps.title: Build ginger sauce
steps.instruction: Simmer soy, mirin, ginger, and garlic until glossy. Finish with sesame oil. Keep warm at 140°F. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Prep proteins
steps.instruction: Pat shrimp and pork belly dry. Season pork belly with salt and pepper; shrimp with pinch of salt. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Preheat the flat-top griddle
steps.instruction: Preheat griddle to 400°F. Oil surface lightly. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Render pork belly
steps.instruction: Griddle pork belly cubes 10–12 minutes until crisp and 165°F internal. Drain excess fat. Hold at 170°F. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Griddle shrimp
steps.instruction: Griddle shrimp at 450°F 2 minutes per side until pink and 140°F. Hold at 170°F separately. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Char vegetables
steps.instruction: Griddle zucchini, mushrooms, and onions at 425°F until charred and tender, 8–10 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Combine at service
steps.instruction: Toss shrimp, pork belly, and veg with ginger sauce at the line. Do not sauced during long hold. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Platter for ten
steps.instruction: Serve mixed grill over fried rice with extra sauce and sesame. About 6 oz protein per firefighter. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: Render pork belly first—shrimp overcooks while belly catches up.
Sauce at the line keeps shrimp from turning rubbery in hold.
Drain belly fat between batches or griddle smokes out the hall.
tonightSpread: Firehall hibachi mixed grill with fried rice.
leftovers: Mixed grill into hibachi fried rice bowls.
Pork belly cubes into ramen next shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Mixed hibachi without the tired chicken-plus-steak combo. Shrimp and pork belly cook at different times but both love the flat-top and hold at 170°F.
mealPrepNotes: Prep proteins separately. Griddle pork belly first at 400°F to render, then shrimp at 450°F, veg last. Hold components covered at 170°F. Sauce at service.
